meaning: The Christian kingdom in East Africa (roughly today's Ethiopia and Eritrea) where early Muslims found refuge. In Arabic, al-Habashah
The call to prayer, announcing that a prayer's time has begun
"One": a name of Allah meaning the One (Q 112:1). Bilal repeated it while he was being tortured
The Hereafter: the life after this one, after death and the Day of Judgment
"Peace be upon him." Said after the name of any prophet other than Muhammad ﷺ, and after the angels' names
"All praise is for Allah." Said for good news, after sneezing, or when asked how you are
The Arabic word for God. Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews use it too
"Allah is the greatest." Said to start the prayer and when moving between positions (also called the takbir)
"O Allah, answer our prayer." Said after al-Fatiha
"The trustworthy": what the people of Makkah called the Prophet ﷺ before his prophethood. (Not the same as *Amin*, said after al-Fatiha)
"The helpers": the Muslims of Madinah who took in the Prophet ﷺ and the emigrants from Makkah
A place near Makkah where people from Madinah met the Prophet ﷺ at night and pledged to protect him
"The farthest": al-Masjid al-Aqsa, the masjid in Jerusalem the Prophet ﷺ was taken to on the Night Journey
"The Especially Merciful": a name of Allah, said in every al-Fatiha
"The Most Merciful," whose mercy covers everything: a name of Allah, said in every al-Fatiha
"The Provider": a name of Allah. Jobs and paychecks are means; He is the source
The plain near Makkah where pilgrims stand in prayer on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah, the heart of Hajj; also the name of that day
"Peace": a name of Allah, free of every flaw and the source of peace
"The Appreciative": a name of Allah, who notices and rewards even small good deeds
The 10th of Muharram, the day Allah saved Musa (Moses) and his people; a recommended fast
The afternoon prayer (4 rak'ahs)
"I ask Allah's forgiveness." Said three times right after every prayer, and any time
"The One who keeps accepting repentance": a name of Allah
The parts of the body that must be covered, in prayer and in public. For men, at least navel to knees; for women, everything except the face, hands and (in the Hanafi school) feet
A verse of the Qur'an (the word also means "sign")
"The Verse of the Throne" (Qur'an 2:255), about Allah's greatness and care. Many recite it after prayers and before sleep
Saying *Bismillahir-rahmanir-rahim* ("In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful"), e.g. before al-Fatiha
"In the name of Allah." Said before starting something, like wudu or eating
The white riding animal that carried the Prophet ﷺ to Jerusalem on the Night Journey
Inviting people to Islam, mostly by example and kind, honest answers, never by pressure
A frame drum, like a tambourine without jingles; scholars differ on instruments, but many allow the daff at weddings and Eid
David: a prophet and king, given the Zabur (Psalms)
Remembering Allah, usually by repeating short phrases like *Subhan Allah*
The midday prayer (4 rak'ahs)
The twelfth month of the Islamic calendar, the month of Hajj and Eid al-Adha
A personal prayer or request to Allah, in any language, at any time
One of the two yearly Muslim celebrations: Eid al-Fitr after Ramadan and Eid al-Adha during Hajj
"The festival of sacrifice" on the 10th of Dhul Hijjah, during Hajj, remembering Ibrahim
"The festival of breaking the fast" on the 1st of Shawwal, right after Ramadan
The dawn prayer (2 rak'ahs), prayed between first light and sunrise
"The Opening": the Qur'an's first chapter, seven short verses recited in every rak'ah
A payment in place of fasting by someone who can never fast (old age, lasting illness): feeding a poor person for each missed day
Islamic law: the detailed rulings on worship and daily life, worked out by scholars
"The Forgiving": a name of Allah
Backbiting: saying something about a person who isn't there that they would hate to hear, even if it's true
A full-body wash done with intention: needed after sex, a wet dream, or the end of a period, and taken when becoming Muslim
A report of what the Prophet ﷺ said, did or approved
Someone who has memorized the whole Qur'an
Hagar: Isma'il's mother, whose search for water between two hills pilgrims retrace in the sa'i
The pilgrimage to Makkah, required once in a lifetime of those who are able
"The Wise": a name of Allah. Nothing He does is without a reason
Allowed. Used especially for food and for meat slaughtered the Islamic way
A study circle: a regular class where people sit together to learn about Islam
Forbidden by Allah
Modesty and a sense of dignity, inside and out. The Prophet ﷺ called it part of faith
Modest covering. Usually means a Muslim woman's head covering, but the idea of modesty applies to men and women
The Prophet's migration from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE, the starting point of the Muslim calendar
The Muslim lunar calendar, counted from the Hijrah
Staying in the masjid for a set time to devote yourself to worship, especially in the last ten days of Ramadan
Satan: one of the jinn, who refused Allah's command. Not a fallen angel
Abraham: a prophet, called "a Muslim" in the Qur'an; the Salat Ibrahimiyya mentions him
The meal that breaks the fast at sunset
The sacred state a pilgrim enters for Hajj or Umrah, with its own rules; men wear two plain white cloths
Excellence in worship: worshipping Allah as though you see Him, knowing He sees you
"Sincerity": the Qur'an's 112th chapter, four short verses saying Allah is One. Often the first surah new Muslims learn to recite after al-Fatiha
Sincerity: doing a deed for Allah alone, not for people's praise
The person who leads the prayer; also a masjid's religious leader and teacher
Faith: believing in Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and His decree
"If Allah wills." Said about plans for the future
The Gospel: the scripture Muslims believe Allah gave to Jesus

term: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un
meaning: "We belong to Allah, and to Him we return." Said on hearing of a death or any loss (Qur'an 2:156)
Jesus, son of Mary: a great prophet and the Messiah in Islam
The night prayer (4 rak'ahs)
Ishmael: a prophet, son of Ibrahim and Hajar, who helped his father raise the Ka'bah
Cleaning the private parts with water (or tissue, then water) after using the toilet
Hell: the place of punishment in the Hereafter, which Allah warns about
Paradise: the garden of joy in the Hereafter, beyond anything we can imagine
The angel Gabriel, who brought the Qur'an to the Prophet ﷺ
"Striving." Mostly the struggle against your own ego and bad habits and striving to do good; in Islamic law it also covers lawful defensive war with strict rules, never attacks on civilians
Unseen beings made from fire, with free will like humans
The Friday midday prayer at the masjid: a sermon, then two rak'ahs. It replaces Dhuhr on Fridays
The cube-shaped house of worship in Makkah that Muslims face in prayer
A leather sock or boot worn after wudu; in the Hanafi school, thick socks that meet the same conditions count too. You can wipe over it instead of washing your feet
A sermon, given by the imam before the Friday prayer (and after the Eid prayers)
"The Subtle, the Gently Kind": a name of Allah, whose kindness often works quietly
The Night of Decree: the night the Qur'an was first revealed, better than a thousand months, sought in the odd nights of Ramadan's last ten
A school of Islamic law. The four main Sunni schools are Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali; all are valid
The sunset prayer (3 rak'ahs)
The marriage gift a groom gives his bride; it belongs to her alone
The city in Arabia where the Ka'bah stands; the place of Hajj and Umrah (often spelled Mecca)
Mary, mother of Jesus. A chapter of the Qur'an is named after her
"This is what Allah willed." Said when admiring something good
A mosque: a place where Muslims pray together
An honorary title for each of the Prophet's ﷺ wives (Q 33:6)
"Those who emigrated": the Muslims who left Makkah for Madinah
The first month of the Muslim year, one of the four sacred months
"The One who answers" (prayers): a name of Allah
Moses: a prophet to whom Allah spoke directly, given the Tawrah (Torah)
A printed copy of the Qur'an in Arabic. Muslims make wudu before touching one
A prophet: someone who receives revelation from Allah
The title of the king of Abyssinia, often written "the Negus" in English. The one who sheltered the Muslims was named Ashamah
An Islamic song, often voice-only
The Islamic marriage contract: both agree freely, with witnesses and a mahr
The minimum amount of savings (measured in gold or silver) above which zakat is due after a lunar year
Intention: the "why" in your heart behind an action, including which prayer you're about to pray
Noah: one of the earliest prophets
Making up a missed obligatory prayer (or fast) later
Allah's decree: nothing happens outside His knowledge and will. The sixth article of faith
"The Near": a name of Allah
The direction of the Ka'bah, which Muslims face to pray. Roughly northeast from most of the US
A special du'a said standing in prayer; in Hanafi witr, said in the third rak'ah before bowing
The holy book of Islam: Allah's words, revealed to the Prophet ﷺ in Arabic over 23 years, in 114 chapters
The Arab tribe that ran Makkah in the Prophet's ﷺ time. He was born into it
One round of the prayer: standing, bowing and two prostrations
The month of fasting, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar
A messenger: a prophet also sent to deliver a message to a people
Interest (and other unfair gain) on loans and certain trades; forbidden in Islam
Showing off: doing worship or good deeds so that people will admire you
The bowing position in prayer, hands on knees
Walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah, part of Hajj and Umrah
Patience: staying steady with Allah in doing good, avoiding wrong, and bearing hardship
Voluntary charity: any amount, any time, even a kind act
The prayer Muslims perform five times a day
"Peace." The greeting *as-salamu 'alaykum* (peace be upon you), and the words that end the prayer
The blessings on the Prophet ﷺ said in the last sitting of the prayer, after the tashahhud; it mentions Ibrahim (Abraham)
The life story of the Prophet ﷺ, told from the early sources
The testimony of faith: "There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Saying it sincerely makes someone Muslim
The tenth month of the Muslim year, which begins with Eid al-Fitr
Worshipping anything besides Allah, or treating a created thing as having powers only He has. The opposite of tawhid
Gratitude: noticing Allah's blessings, thanking Him, and using them well
"The one who affirms the truth": the title of Abu Bakr
A twig used to clean the teeth. The Prophet ﷺ loved to use it
"Glory be to Allah." Said in amazement, and as dhikr
The pre-dawn meal before a day of fasting
Prostration: forehead, nose, hands, knees and toes on the ground
The forgetfulness prostration: two extra prostrations at the end of a prayer that repair a required part missed by mistake
The Prophet's way ﷺ: what he did, said and approved. Also used for acts that are recommended but not required
A chapter of the Qur'an. There are 114
Saying *Allahu akbar*
The takbir said after each obligatory prayer from Fajr on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah to Asr on the 13th (necessary in the Hanafi school)
The pilgrim's call, *Labbayk Allahumma labbayk* ("Here I am, O Allah, here I am"), said throughout Hajj and Umrah
The extra night prayer of Ramadan, prayed in pairs of rak'ahs after Isha, usually at the masjid
The words said in the sitting of the prayer, starting *at-tahiyyatu lillah* and ending with the shahada
Walking around the Ka'bah seven times in worship, part of Hajj and Umrah
Trusting Allah with the outcome after doing your part ("tie your camel, then trust Allah")
Repentance: turning back to Allah with regret, stopping the wrong, and asking His forgiveness
Allah's oneness: one God, with no partner or equal, who alone is worshipped
The Torah: the scripture Allah gave to Musa (Moses)
Dry purification with clean earth or stone, used in place of wudu or ghusl when there's no water or water would cause harm
The animal sacrificed for Allah on Eid al-Adha or the days after it (also called qurbani)
The "lesser pilgrimage" to Makkah: ihram, tawaf, sa'i and cutting the hair. It can be done any time of year
"The Loving": a name of Allah
A woman's marriage guardian: a trustworthy Muslim man who looks out for her and checks a suitor. The imam can help converts find one
Nagging, repeated doubts (often about wudu or prayer). The cure is to go with what you're sure of
A short prayer after Isha and before dawn. Hanafi: required, 3 rak'ahs; other schools: strongly recommended
The short wash before prayer: hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head, feet
Meat slaughtered the Islamic way, with Allah's name said
The Psalms: the scripture Allah gave to Dawud (David)
The yearly required charity: a set share (usually 2.5%) of savings above a minimum, given to people in need
The small set charity given for each person before the Eid al-Fitr prayer, so the poor can celebrate too
The well beside the Ka'bah in Makkah. Pilgrims still drink its water
Sex outside marriage; the Qur'an says not even to go near it
*Sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*: "peace and blessings be upon him." Said or written after the Prophet Muhammad's name
